title: The last small ones the register still holds
description: What the register still holds after the release phases: an ownership check that discards half the identity it was given, a document pair that contradicts each other about how many tiers a lock has, a fixture that aborts a suite on a platform this project supports, a hook paragraph repeated once per tool result in a batch, a derivation that is silently inert under a symlinked path, and two hand-maintained lists that opt a new caller out by being forgotten. None is user-visible today and every one of them is a check or a sentence somebody will trust the next time they need it.
desiredOutcome: Every open entry in the register that is not an explicit out-of-scope decision is either closed by code or restated as a decision with its own trigger.

tasks.title: A release names the run, and a taker's identity is checked whole
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: the release path checks the whole identity a claim records, not half of it. Ownership is compared on the session alone while the take records a process as well and the release is handed one it then ignores, so two measurements inside one session cannot be told apart: the loser's release succeeds and drops a lock out from under a run that still holds it. This is the same class the takeover repair closed from the other end, and it is the last door in that file where an identity is recorded and not read. The age rule stays, because it is the fallback when no identity was recorded at all.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__locks.py: a release from a different process of the same session is refused, and a release from the process that took it is allowed

outcome.technical: _release_conflict compares session and process, each only where the claim recorded it and it resolves, and accepts the two candidate processes so the ordinary in-process take and release is unaffected.
outcome.descriptive: A release is refused when the identity it carries disagrees with the one the claim recorded, on either field rather than on the session alone.

tasks.title: A suite does not abort on a platform this project supports
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: no case in this suite can abort the body on a platform the project supports, and the smaller findings on the same surface are closed with it. One fixture makes the lock path a directory, which one platform reports as the name already existing and another as a permission refusal - only the first is caught, so on the second the escape takes that case and the ones after it out of the run. The class is the one this release already repaired elsewhere: a case that reports by raising takes its neighbours down and a harness reads one crash as a column of checks.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__locks.py: a lock path that cannot be created for a reason this platform words differently is still one answer, and the cases after it still run

outcome.technical: _link_into_place asks whether the name exists before attempting the raw create, so the two platform wordings collapse to one meaning; a case forces the other platform's wording directly rather than waiting to be run there.
outcome.descriptive: A name a directory occupies is one fact on every platform, rather than whichever errno the local create call raises.

tasks.title: Two documents agree about how many tiers the lock has
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: no document states a count of lock tiers that the library contradicts, and the statement is checked rather than remembered. The build guide says the command runs over two tiers while the command's own docstring says three, so two documents now contradict each other about a vocabulary the library declares in one place. The repair is not to correct the number: it is to read the vocabulary from where it is declared, the way the claim anchors already hold every other sentence in that family, so the next tier added cannot leave a document behind.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__areas.py: the tier vocabulary a document states is the one the library declares, read from both sides

outcome.technical: a list anchor reads FIXED_NAMES and checks it against the orchestration document, through the mechanism that already holds the other lists in that family; both documents lost the count and gained the name they were missing.
outcome.descriptive: Neither document states a count of lock tiers, and the sentence that names them is derived from the library's own list.

tasks.title: A hook paragraph is carried once per turn, not once per file
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: a batch of edits does not paste the same paragraph into the model's context once per file, and the invariant check stops on a breach the gate did not cover. Hook context is appended to every tool result, so twelve edits carry twelve copies of one paragraph - which is the same defect this release already repaired for the plan gate's own notice, reached through a different door: the repair there was per session, and a batch inside one turn is the case it does not cover. The second half is smaller and of a piece: the invariant check stops on a red gate but not on a breach the gate never asked about, so the louder failure hides the quieter one.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_require_plan.py: a batch of edits in one turn carries the advisory paragraph once and a count, and a new turn carries it again

outcome.technical: The TDD reminder keeps session state for whether the full template has already ridden; the first file in a session gets it, every later one gets a pointer, and the verdict stays warn in both cases.
outcome.descriptive: A batch of edits carries the advisory's full text once instead of once per file, without silencing it.

tasks.title: The reuse identity resolves both sides of its own comparison
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: the set of paths the recorder writes is computed the same way whichever spelling of the project path the caller used, and a narrowing that did not apply is said rather than silently skipped. The comparison resolves one side and not the other, so on a machine where any component of the project path is a symbolic link the manifest falls out of the exclusion, is read into the content identity, changes on every recorded run, and the whole reuse feature is inert - with nothing but a count in a basis line to tell the two behaviours apart. It fails safe here by luck rather than by design: more of the tree stays inside the identity, so the answer is measure again. The comparison is still wrong, and the next reader to rely on it may not be so lucky.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__evidence_io.py: a project whose path reaches the same tree through a symbolic link excludes the same paths as one that does not, and the basis says when an exclusion the caller asked for was dropped

outcome.descriptive: Cancelled: moved to P56.5, which owns whether the reuse saving is real; the defect is the same one and splitting it across two phases would put one repair behind two sign-offs

tasks.title: Two lists that opt a new caller out by being forgotten
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: neither list of call sites is maintained by hand, and the derivation that replaces them carries a floor so an empty answer is a failure rather than a pass. A new caller of the lock's acquire path was invisible to the lint that grades those sites until somebody added it by hand, which is precisely the failure this project keeps recording one surface over: a row added later opts out by being forgotten. The third piece is the warning class the doctor cannot collapse, because its body quotes the offending text so every line differs after the locator - grouping on the rule rather than the body is the repair, and it needs a rule identifier at each emission site, which is the field that module was built without.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__output.py: the call sites a lint grades are derived from the tree with a floor, so a pattern that stops matching fails rather than reporting nothing to fix

outcome.descriptive: Cancelled: Split after its first attempt, because the task carried two pieces with different answers and one record cannot say both. The derivation of the two hand-kept lists is real and continues as P55.8. The third piece - grouping the doctor's quoting warning class on a rule id rather than on the body - re-opens a decision that _warning_groups.py records with its reasoning and test__warning_groups.py pins, no revisit trigger has fired, and its cost is a new field at every emission site across the manifest, panel, status and deps surfaces to merge lines that differ in the one part the reader has to read. Declined on the record rather than carried as open work.

tasks.title: The report's copy interaction is observed, or the gate says which it could not observe
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: the interactive gate is green, and whichever of the two causes it was is stated. RELEASE BLOCKER: the gate is red on two clipboard interactions and red identically on the committed bytes, so it is not a recent change. The message is the finding rather than the failure - it says two assertion sites never RAN, so the report was graded on work that did not happen, which is the class this release repaired twice inside the suites, and the gate already refuses to call that a pass. Two questions come before any code, in this order: does the copy still work for a person, and does the automation hold the clipboard permission a headless context needs. A copy that works for a human and cannot be observed is a harness repair; a copy that has stopped working is a product defect and a much larger one. The gate cannot tell those apart today and saying which is part of the fix. What must not move is the refusal to grade a report on assertions that never ran: widening it to pass on an unreachable site turns the one instrument that can see this into one that cannot.

add: tools/check-report-interactive.mjs: an assertion site that cannot be reached is reported as unreached with the reason, apart from one that ran and disagreed

outcome.technical: selectRun's clipboard fallback selected its payload by a class belonging to the other caller of the shared helper, so the sha button's fallback matched nothing; it now selects the sibling payload by shape. The worked example gained a task carrying a commit that resolves, so the two assertion sites the gate reported as never reached now run.
outcome.descriptive: The copy button's fallback reaches the value it was asked to copy, and the report gate grades work that actually ran.

tasks.title: Two lists that opt a new member out by being forgotten
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: neither hand-kept list of call sites in tests/test__output.py is maintained by hand, and the derivation that replaces each carries a floor so an empty answer is a failure rather than a pass. Two lists sit in that file: px2's _publishers, the modules that may not call os.path.relpath directly, and lk4's _lk_callers, the callers of the lock's acquire path. A new caller of acquire was invisible to lk4 until somebody added it by hand, which is precisely the failure this project keeps recording one surface over: a row added later opts out by being forgotten. Both lists are walked from the tree instead, each keeping the sentinel it already carries so a file that cannot be read stays a finding rather than an exception, and each with a floor that fails when the derivation returns nothing.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__output.py: the call sites each lint grades are derived from the tree with a floor, so a derivation that stops matching fails rather than reporting nothing to fix

outcome.technical: lk4's membership is a walk over M.py_files(M.SCRIPTS_DIR) keeping any file whose non-comment lines spell _locks.acquire(, with the unreadable-file sentinel generalised to any walked file and a floor asserted with >= rather than a tally. The walk found two callers the retired tuple never named.
outcome.descriptive: The callers a case grades are found by reading the tree rather than by somebody remembering, and a walk that stops matching fails instead of reporting nothing to fix.

tasks.title: A case that says it pins the window plants its decoy where the window cannot reach
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: widening _areas._CLAIM_WINDOW past the section reddens a case. It does not today - the constant was raised past any document in the tree and the whole sweep stayed green, so the one site that reads it is defended by nothing. oa12 carries a comment asserting the window is load-bearing and that oa12 is what says so, and that comment is the reason nobody looked: it plants its decoy BEFORE the anchor's bullet, while the slice runs forward from the anchor, so no forward widening can ever reach it. What oa12 pins is the slice's left endpoint, which the slice does for free. Add a second laundered document with the decoy planted after the anchor and outside the shipped window, a finding at the shipped value and a non-finding only once the window is widened past it. oa12 stays as it is - a decoy behind the anchor is worth a case, it just is not this one - and the comment above it stops claiming what the new case is the one to claim.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__areas.py: a claim satisfied only by a neighbour's value BEYOND the context window is a finding, so widening the window reddens the case

outcome.technical: oa33 launders the document with the decoy planted past the shipped window from the anchor, so it is a finding at the shipped width and stops being one once the constant is widened; oa12 is unchanged and its comment now says it pins the slice's left endpoint.
outcome.descriptive: The window's width is pinned by a case that reddens when it grows, and the case that could not pin it says what it does pin.

tasks.title: A persisted path goes through the one helper, and the table that says so names it
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: scripts/manifest/repair-commits.py builds the relative path it persists through _output.posix_rel rather than by hand, and px2's publisher table names the file. The value it writes today is right, because the hand-rolled spelling happens to be what the helper does - so nothing is broken and nothing will be until the next copy leaves the separator replacement off, which is the defect the helper was written after. The table that would have caught it does not name this file. THE TABLE STAYS HAND-KEPT ON THE RECORD: whether a value is published is a judgement about what happens to it downstream, not a fact the tree states, and one file in this tree holds both a containment check that must NOT go through the helper and a published path that must, so a file-level derivation would be unsound in both directions.

outcome.technical: repair-commits.py builds the persisted relative path with _output.posix_rel, and px2's publisher tuple names the file with a comment giving the concrete reason the table is not derived.
outcome.descriptive: A path written into the trail goes through the one helper, and the table that enforces that names the writer.

tasks.title: Two rows in the mutation table credit what they did not prove
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: the full red-first sweep exits clean, and neither of the two rows that do not prove their gate is repaired by renaming a file or a case. THE NAVIGABILITY ROW drops one section marker from a named file, which reports something only when that file satisfies two constraints at once - the rule applies to it, AND it carries exactly the minimum number of markers, because a file with more still has enough after one is dropped. The target drifted in the second constraint and the gate reports STAYED GREEN; the comment above the row narrates the same failure happening in the FIRST constraint the previous time, which is why another file name is not the repair. Derive the target: a file the rule applies to that carries exactly the minimum, refusing loudly when the tree holds none, because a sweep that cannot find a subject has to say so rather than report a colour. THE DICT-KEY ROW deletes the producer's key from the gate runner, which trips the floor case - that case names that exact producer and key and asserts membership - before the rule under test has anything to report, so the sweep credits a case it did not observe. Relabelling makes the sweep honest and leaves the rule unproven; the mutation has to break the READER side instead, a read of a key nothing writes, which is the shape the credited case is the only one to catch.

outcome.technical: The navigability row derives its target by walking for a file the rule applies to that carries exactly the minimum markers, simulating the drop before accepting it and raising when none qualifies; the dict-key row mutates a resolved reader's lookup instead of the producer's key.
outcome.descriptive: Both rows now redden the case they credit, and the one that named a file by hand asks the tree instead.

tasks.title: The sibling writer's persisted path goes through the same helper
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: scripts/manifest/repair-tests-add.py builds the relative path it records into the trail through _output.posix_rel rather than by hand, and px2's publisher table names it. It is the second instance of the same defect: the value is right today because the hand-rolled spelling happens to be what the helper does, and nothing breaks until a copy leaves the separator fix off. The behavioural suite cannot see it on this platform, because the two spellings produce the same string there - the source-level rule is the only thing that can, which is why the table has to name the file.

outcome.technical: repair-tests-add.py builds the persisted relative path with _output.posix_rel, matching its twin's call site, and px2's publisher tuple names the file.
outcome.descriptive: The second writer's path into the trail goes through the one helper, and the table that enforces that names it.

tasks.title: The mutating sweep refuses to overwrite work the tree has not committed
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: tools/prove-gates.py will not mutate a file the tree has not committed without being told to. It copies a file, mutates it, and copies the original back, which is right when nothing else is writing. Two things go wrong when something is: an edit made between the copy and the restore is overwritten by the restore - REASONED, not observed, and not to be written down as though it happened - and, which DID happen, the sweep's own mid-run mutation shows in git status and is indistinguishable from the work of the agent whose worktree it is. Agent progress is read from the worktree here because a transcript does not grow, so a sweep running in that worktree silently suspends the one signal the orchestrator trusts; it was read wrong, acted on, and reported to the user as destroyed work that never existed. A file about to be mutated that is dirty is a refusal naming the file, with a deliberate way past it for the case where the dirt IS what is being proven.

add: tools/prove-gates.py: a row whose target is dirty is refused by name rather than mutated, and the refusal can be overridden deliberately

outcome.technical: redfirst.sh asks git for the file's own state before taking its backup and refuses with the file named when it differs from HEAD or is untracked, failing loud when git cannot be asked; --allow-dirty is the deliberate bypass and the EXIT/TERM/INT restore is unchanged.
outcome.descriptive: The script that mutates a file to prove a check refuses one it did not write, so its own mid-run state can never be mistaken for somebody's work.

tasks.title: The evidence writer persists a path with no separator fix at all
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: both hand-rolled relative paths in the evidence writer go through _output.posix_rel, and px2's publisher table names the file. TWO SITES, NOT THE SAME SEVERITY. One repeats the hand-rolled spelling the helper exists to replace, which is correct today and wrong the day a copy drops the separator fix - the same class as the two writers already repaired. The other applies NO separator fix at all and persists the result into a stored config under the key every other reader expects to hold a manifest path: on a platform whose separator is not the forward slash it writes the platform's spelling into a value the product compares against manifest paths, which are stored with forward slashes. That is a wrong value on a supported platform, not a duplication. Nothing caught it because the rule reads a hand-kept table this file is not in, and the behavioural suites cannot see it on this platform at all, since both spellings produce the same string here - so it is invisible to the source rule by omission and to the behavioural rule by platform.

outcome.technical: Both hand-rolled relative paths in _evidence_io go through _output.posix_rel - the one compared against version-control output and the one persisted as the stored manifest path - and px2's publisher tuple names the file.
outcome.descriptive: The evidence writer spells a persisted path the way every other writer does, and the rule that enforces that finally names it.

tasks.title: The write guard reads the command's own working directory before it resolves a target
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: the shell-write arm of the secrets guard resolves a relative write target against the directory the command actually ran in, and withdraws when it cannot establish one. Driven three ways today: a relative file name written from a directory outside the repository is BLOCKED with the refusal naming a repository-relative path that does not exist; the same command with an explicit change of directory first is also blocked; the same write with an absolute path outside the repository is allowed. The verdict turns on how the path was spelled rather than on where it lands, which is this register's longest-running defect class. The sibling post-hook already reads that working directory and carries a whole message for a command that ran in another tree; this hook contains no reference to it. The helper that decides whether a destination is resolvable already withdraws on expansions, substitutions, globs and a home shorthand, because those cannot be resolved from the text - a bare relative name cannot either, without the working directory the payload carries.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_guard_secrets_read.py: a relative write target is resolved against the command's own working directory, and a write landing outside the repository is not refused as though it were inside

outcome.technical: The shell-write arm resolves a relative target against the directory the command ran in, following every change-of-directory clause, and withdraws into the existing unresolvable-destination path when that cannot be established; the manifest comparison three lines away got the same repair.
outcome.descriptive: The guard decides on where a write lands rather than on how its path was spelled.

tasks.title: The write guard's interpreter arms match the interpreters its refusal names
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: every interpreter the guard's refusal text names has a write arm, and the KNOWN LIMIT note names what is still uncovered. One interpreter's three-argument open and its in-place edit flag - the direct twin of the stream editor's in-place flag, which is covered - both drive ALLOW today, while the refusal lists that interpreter among the forms it claims to watch. The post-hook still reports the file afterwards, so the write is not invisible; what is missing is the block, which is the difference between a guard and a notice. A limit a guard states is a limit a reader can work with; a limit it does not state reads as coverage.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_guard_secrets_read.py: the interpreters the refusal names and the interpreters the expression set covers are the same set

outcome.technical: The in-place flag is read out of a bundle for every interpreter the refusal names, including the backup-suffix form, plus a three-argument open arm; the case-insensitivity is scoped to the interpreter name so an include-path flag is not read as the in-place one.
outcome.descriptive: Every interpreter the refusal names is watched, in the spelling people actually write.

tasks.title: The gate's note stops naming a command that refuses when the declaring task is done
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: the plan gate's explanatory note tells a reader of a DONE task's file the route the sign-off procedure actually mandates. It has one branch for a file whose declaring task is not running and it assumes that task is merely unstarted, so against a done task it says the task has not been started, that starting it is the route, and - in its last clause - not to add a second task for a file the plan already declares. Driven: starting a done task exits non-zero and refuses, and adding a task is exactly what phase sign-off now mandates. The refusal names a command that refuses, asserts a state that is false, and forbids the correct route. That function's own docstring says it exists because a refusal naming a remedy its reader cannot reach is a fault already paid for twice here.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_require_plan.py: the note for a file declared by a DONE task names the add route and does not tell the reader to start it

outcome.technical: _declaration_note gained a branch for a declaring task in a terminal status, routing both audiences to the add-then-run sequence phase sign-off mandates instead of to a start verb that refuses.
outcome.descriptive: The refusal names a route its reader can take.

tasks.title: A blocked tool call is a stop-and-report, whatever tool was blocked
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: the executor's own brief carries a flat rule that a blocked tool call is never a signal to reach for a different tool, stated about TOOLS rather than about an adjacent file. What it says today is that a refusal is the executor's instruction and that it must not put the change somewhere else - correct, and scoped to an adjacent file and to relocating a change. The only do-not-work-around sentence in the agent and reference documents sits in a bullet about secrets, so an executor reading it as scoped to secrets is not obviously misreading. An operator watched an executor meet a hard block on one tool and finish the work through another; the outcome was correct, which is what makes it the kind of workaround that becomes habit.

outcome.technical: audit-executor.md carries a rule that a blocked tool call is never a signal to reach for a different tool, and states that it is not mechanised, naming what the prohibition checker reads and what the related hook actually does.
outcome.descriptive: A blocked tool call is a stop-and-report, whatever tool was blocked - stated, and honest about not being enforced.

tasks.title: The prose refusal marks the span it matched and stops naming a cause it never tested
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: the refusal that rejects a brief on argv says what it actually matched, and the caller can tell a ternary from a lost substitution. The check reads five whitespace-adjacency shapes and tests for no backtick at all; the message volunteers command substitution as the explanation, which is why a report of it named a cause that was not present. It already prints a window around the hit - what is missing is a marker INSIDE that window pointing at the character that matched. Measured over this project's own plan, one hit in over a thousand prose strings, and that one a run of spaces: the false-positive rate against ordinary prose is near zero and the class that misfires is CODE QUOTED INTO PROSE, which is what a plan imported from an engineering report carries. The stdin escape is real and drives clean, and it is documented under the framing IF THE BRIEF CONTAINS BACKTICKS - which an operator whose text has none reads as somebody else's problem. The flag's own help text says nothing at all.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: the refusal marks the matched span and states the shape it matched rather than a substitution it did not test for

tasks.title: A verb that writes another phase's shard says which branch that phase is on
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: a verb writing a shard names the target phase's branch when it differs from the one the caller is standing on, and the document stops promising more than the layout delivers. Every script that writes a shard was swept: none prints branch context. The nearest thing compares TREES rather than branches, which is why it stays silent on the case that bit - same tree, two branches, one shard, a real merge conflict in the file the layout exists to keep conflict-free. A warning, not a refusal: naming it is the whole fix, because the writer then knows to expect a merge. NOT the same shape as the commit-scope check, which starts from commits the plan records and asks what each staged; this starts from a path and asks a containment question about commits the plan records nowhere. And note before designing the condition: fewer than a fifth of this project's own phases carry a branch at all and every running one has none, so a check keyed only on a populated branch would be silent in the dogfood. The document's sentence about a phase run touching only its own shard gains the boundary the verbs cross.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: writing a shard whose phase names a different branch than the caller stands on prints that, and writing one that does not is silent

tasks.title: The verb that dirties the index says what to do about it, and the tool that lands it is findable
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: the verb that writes both the shard and the index says that the index is now dirty and names the tool that lands it, and that tool is discoverable before the mistake rather than only in the refusal that follows it. The first-order trap is already closed - the commit step no longer asks for a hand-composed pathspec and the script refuses when the index is staged. What is unchanged is the silence at the moment the state is created. The second-order failure was reproduced in a scratch repository: file a task mid-run, commit by hand, and the manifest AT that commit does not validate - the index names a task whose shard is not in it - with the invariants reporting both breaches against the recorded commit. Anyone checking out that commit gets an invalid plan. The tool that already does the right thing is named in no command page, no reference document, no agent brief and not in the README; the only place its name reaches a human is the refusal that fires after the mistake.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: a verb that leaves the index dirty says so and names the tool that lands it

tasks.title: The citation scanner's own suite carries strays outside its fixture zone
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: the suite that holds the citation scanner's fixtures carries register ids ONLY inside those fixtures, and the exemption row's named cost shrinks to what it has to be. The row exempts the whole file because a text scanner can only be shown to fire by handing it the literal it must recognise - true of the fixture zone and of nothing else. Outside it the file carries stray citations in comments about unrelated test families, which the row itself names as its accepted cost rather than hiding. Clear those, and leave the fixtures alone. Consider whether the exemption can be narrowed from the file to the region that needs it, and if it cannot, say why in the row rather than widening the silence.

outcome.technical: Every register citation outside test__deps.py's fixture block is rewritten as the constraint it stood in for, the fixtures are untouched, and the exemption row records that and why the exemption cannot be narrowed below a whole file.
outcome.descriptive: The scanner's own suite carries ids only where a scanner can be shown to fire, and the row says so.

verifiedBy: the scan functions called directly over the file with no exemption

tasks.title: The plan gate judges an edit inside a worktree of the project it is guarding
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: an edit landing in a git worktree of the project is judged by the plan gate, and a tree the gate cannot place is a refusal to answer rather than a silent allow. DRIVEN ACROSS THREE TREES with the change large enough to clear the gate's own trivial-change slot: an edit in the main checkout denies, an edit in a worktree denies when the project directory names that worktree, and the SAME edit ALLOWS SILENTLY when the project directory names the main checkout - which is the shape a real session runs in, since the project directory is the checkout the session started in and the agent works in a worktree of it. The gate resolves the manifest from the project directory, the file sits under a different root, and it is never judged: no refusal, no advisory, nothing. This is the same root-resolution question the write guard's relative-path repair just answered, one hook over, and the repair there is the model - read where the thing actually is rather than assuming it sits under one root. It matters more here than anywhere because the gate exists so a subagent cannot wander outside the plan, and a worktree is the recommended way to run one. ONE THING IS UNEXPLAINED AND MUST NOT BE GUESSED AT: one of the two worktrees driven allowed the edit in every configuration, including with its own project directory and its own copy of the hook, where its sibling denied. Establish why before designing, and if it turns out to be a second cause, say so.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_require_plan.py: an edit inside a worktree of the project is judged, and a tree the gate cannot place is refused rather than allowed in silence
